title: Corneal Collagen Cross-Linking (CXL): Clinical Mastery
summary: CXL is the gold-standard therapeutic intervention for halting the progression of keratoconus and other corneal ectasias by increasing biomechanical rigidity via riboflavin-UVA photopolymerization. This guide outlines the comprehensive clinical protocols, patient selection criteria, and landmark evidence-based management strategies.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: CXL utilizes exogenous Riboflavin (Vitamin B2) as a photosensitizer and Ultraviolet A (UVA, 370 nm) light to induce the formation of covalent bonds (cross-links) between collagen fibrils in the corneal stroma. The reaction is driven by the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS), specifically singlet oxygen, which creates stable bridges between collagen type I molecules. This results in a permanent increase in the biomechanical stiffness of the cornea by approximately 300-450%.

sections.title: Indications & Candidacy
content: Documented progressive keratoconus (e.g., Kmax increase >1.0D over 12 months).
Young age (<18 years) often mandates immediate prophylactic CXL due to aggressive progression.

sections.title: The Dresden Protocol (Standard)
content: Step 1: Corneal epithelial debridement (8-9 mm diameter).
Step 2: Riboflavin 0.1% drops (Isotonic) instilled every 2-3 minutes for 30 minutes (soaking phase).
Step 3: Slit-lamp check for complete stromal saturation (yellow flare in the AC).
Step 4: UVA irradiation (370 nm) at 3 mW/cm² for 30 minutes (total energy 5.4 J/cm²).

rows: Inferior steepening, central thinning, Vogt striae.

sections.title: Red Flags & Contraindications
content: Corneal thickness <400 microns (thinner corneas require hypo-osmolar riboflavin or custom treatment).

content.explanation: S: Soak Riboflavin, T: Thickness check, I: Irradiation (UVA), F: Follow-up frequent, F: Fixate (patient compliance).

sections.title: Recent Advances
content: Accelerated CXL: Higher intensity (9mW/cm² for 10 min) maintains efficacy with reduced chair time.
Transepithelial (Epi-on) CXL: Utilizing riboflavin enhancers (e.g., BAC) to bypass debridement and reduce pain.
Iontophoresis-assisted Riboflavin delivery: Improves stromal saturation speed.
Combined CXL+PRK (Athens Protocol): Used for visual rehabilitation in stable/stabilized ectatic eyes.

rows: Increase steroid frequency, rule out infection.
Bandage contact lens, lubrication, halt steroids.
